Solution 3 is correct. The perimeter of R is the arc length of the outer loop, not of the whole curve.

**Speed.** Differentiating gives f'(θ) = i e^{iθ}(1+e^{iθ})², so |f'(θ)| = |1+e^{iθ}|² = 2 + 2cos θ = 4cos²(θ/2).

**Self-intersection.** Let ω = e^{2πi/3}. Then f(2π/3) = ω + ω² + 1/3 = −1 + 1/3 = −2/3. Since f(4π/3) is the conjugate of f(2π/3) and −2/3 is real, f(4π/3) = −2/3 as well. So the curve crosses itself at −2/3. There is also a cusp at θ = π, where f(π) = −1/3.

**Why the total arc length is wrong.** The part of the curve with θ in [2π/3, 4π/3] forms a small inner loop, and it lies inside the outer loop. The region enclosed by the curve is the interior of the outer loop, so only the outer loop's arc length counts toward the perimeter. Solutions 1 and 2 integrate over the whole curve and get 4π, which includes the inner loop. That is incorrect.

**Outer loop length.** The outer loop is θ ∈ [0, 2π/3] ∪ [4π/3, 2π]. By the symmetry f(2π−θ) = conj f(θ), the two pieces have equal length, so

L = 2∫₀^{2π/3} (2 + 2cos θ) dθ = 4[θ + sin θ]₀^{2π/3} = 4(2π/3 + √3/2) = 8π/3 + 2√3 ≈ 11.84.

This matches Solution 3 (and agrees with the known answer to this problem as I recall it).

CHOICE: 3
